       ex-balanced-triple-for-the-two-dimensional-quantum-sl-two-module]

**Objective.** This companion page works the globalization machinery of
[[balanced-triples-and-global-crystal-bases]] on the smallest concrete
instances and on the exact boundaries of its hypotheses. Every item is a
dependency leaf: nothing outside this page depends on it, and every
computation is a finite Laurent-polynomial or crystal-string calculation.

## What the examples show

- [[ex-canonical-global-basis-normalization-in-symmetric-type]] matches
  four normalizations that are easy to conflate: in rank one the lower
  global vectors are the divided powers $F^{(n)}$ with Kashiwara norm
  $1/[n]_{q^2}!$, transported Lusztig norm
  $\prod_r(1-q^{2r})^{-1}$, ordinary-power factor $[n]_q!$ and Drinfeld
  generator scalar $1/(q-q^{-1})$; in type $A_2$ degree
  $\alpha_1+\alpha_2$ it exhibits the exact lower vectors $F_1F_2,F_2F_1$
  with Gram matrix $\begin{pmatrix}1&q\\q&1\end{pmatrix}$ and its genuine
  non-unimodular inverse-Gram duals.
- [[ex-lower-and-upper-global-bases-in-a-small-highest-weight-module]]
  computes both global bases of the rank-one module $V(m\omega)$ from the
  diagonal norms $d_{m,n}=q^{n(m-n)}\binom{m}{n}_q$. For $m=2$ the upper
  lattice $M_A^\vee=Aw_0\oplus A(1+q^2)^{-1}w_1\oplus Aw_2$ properly
  contains the lower lattice, with middle quotient $A/(1+q^2)$; the two
  lattices share one $A_0$ crystal lattice and the adjoint bar is the one
  fixing the upper basis.

## What the counterexamples show

- [[cex-bar-invariance-and-mod-q-congruence-without-balancedness]] gives
  two witnesses that bar invariance plus a nonzero crystal residue do not
  suffice: the mixed lattice $L'=A_0(v+w)\oplus qA_0v$ in the
  two-dimensional $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-module has balanced part
  $\mathbb Z(v+w)$ and misses the residue class of $qv$, and in the trivial
  module the valid crystal lattice $q^{-1}A_0v$ has two distinct bar-fixed
  integral lifts $(q+q^{-1})v$ and $(q+q^{-1})v+v$ of the same class. The
  integral balanced map, not bar invariance alone, is what the uniqueness
  theorem uses.
- [[ex-balanced-triple-for-the-two-dimensional-quantum-sl-two-module]]
  performs the positive computation on the same module: the balanced
  triple $V_A=Av\oplus Aw$ with its shifted chart residues, the exact
  quasi-$R$ $\Theta=1+(q-q^{-1})E\otimes F$, the tensor bar values, the
  corrected tensor global basis $vv,vw,wv+qvw,ww$, and the contrast with
  the nonbalanced mixed lattice $L'$ whose bar-fixed vector $v+w$ cannot
  be globalized onto the class of $qv$.

Together the four items calibrate the main page: they show the exact
convention dictionary, the genuine difference between the two integral
lattices, and the two ways in which a naive lattice or a naive lift fails,
while the balanced globalization theorem retains its full strength.

**Objective.** This page builds the cyclotomic quotient of a quiver Hecke (KLR)
algebra at a dominant integral weight and proves the highest-weight
categorification statements attached to it. The first-strand relation
$a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)=0$ of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]] is fixed once and for all,
with right-append induction as in
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]]; the entire page is
written in that side convention, and the word-mirror involution
[[lem-word-mirror-involution-of-a-klr-algebra-and-the-quantum-star]] records
the dictionary with the opposite one. On that foundation the page proves the
mixed relations and the projectivity/exactness of the descended functors
([[lem-generic-klr-induction-and-restriction-mixed-relations]],
[[thm-cyclotomic-klr-induction-is-projective-on-the-right]]), the categorical
$\mathfrak{sl}_2$ commutator with its explicit shifts
([[thm-cyclotomic-klr-sl-two-categorical-commutator]]), the finite-dimensional
graded symmetric structure with its trace degree
([[thm-cyclotomic-klr-algebras-are-finite-dimensional-graded-symmetric]]), the
normalized integrable quantum action on both Grothendieck groups
([[lem-cyclotomic-normalized-functors-give-an-integrable-quantum-action]],
[[thm-cyclotomic-klr-functors-define-an-integrable-quantum-action-on-k-zero-and-g-zero]]),
the identification of projective $K_0$ with the integral highest-weight module
and of $G_0$ with its restricted dual
([[thm-cyclotomic-klr-projective-k-zero-is-the-integral-highest-weight-module]],
[[thm-cyclotomic-klr-module-g-zero-is-the-dual-integral-highest-weight-module]]),
and the crystal identification $B(\Lambda)$ for the normalized simple and
projective-cover graphs
([[thm-simple-and-indecomposable-projective-crystals-agree-with-b-lambda]]).

**Proof-tool layer.** Two formal proof tools are carried locally rather than
imported as axioms: the minimal-parabolic diagram proof category
[[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]] with its graded polynomial
flag model
([[lem-minimal-parabolic-polynomial-flag-model-realizes-the-graded-diagram-relations]]),
PBW/bubble normal form
([[lem-minimal-parabolic-diagrams-have-pbw-bubble-normal-form]]) and cap-off
identification
([[lem-cyclotomic-cap-off-quotient-has-no-extra-downward-relations]]); and the
word-mirror involution above. The formal $H_i$ is normalized projective
restriction with its input-weight shift, distinct from the basic restriction
$E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$, and every statement records which of the two is meant.

**Conditional global-basis layer.** The three items
[[lem-cyclotomic-extension-of-scalars-respects-the-based-quotient]],
[[thm-self-dual-indecomposable-cyclotomic-klr-projectives-give-the-lower-global-basis]]
and
[[thm-self-dual-simple-cyclotomic-klr-modules-give-the-upper-global-basis]]
are conditional on the generic geometric global theorem of the parent KLR page
and are kept separate from the unconditional cyclotomic results; their
statements record the normalizations, the $\pi_\Lambda\circ*$ side convention
and the surviving-cover non-merging, and they are not used to prove anything
else on this page.

**Scope and dependence.** The page depends on the divided-power integral forms
of [[balanced-triples-and-global-crystal-bases]] for the lower and upper global
bases, on [[klr-algebras-induction-and-quantum-serre-categorification]] for the
generic KLR algebra, induction bimodules, PBW and negative-half
categorification, on [[grothendieck-groups-and-graded-cartan-pairings]] for the
graded Grothendieck and Cartan-pairing conventions, and on
[[quantum-affine-type-a-and-level-one-fock-space]] for the affine/level-one
context in which the general parameters are used. The Axiom of Choice is inherited through the declared quantum and generic
suppliers of the integral projective identification, restricted-dual
identification, crystal comparison and conditional global-basis layer. The
finite cyclotomic polynomial, quotient and rank-one computations introduce no
further choice.

**Objective.** This page globalizes integral crystal bases at the level of
the divided-power form $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$. Its central objects are the
**balanced triples** of Kashiwara's chart lemma: a spanning $A$-submodule
$M$, a zero chart $L_0$ over $A_0$, an infinity chart $L_\infty$ over
$A_\infty$, and the requirement that the integral balanced intersection
$M\cap L_0\cap L_\infty$ map isomorphically onto the integral residue
$(M\cap L_0)/(M\cap qL_0)$. On that foundation the page constructs the
lower and upper global bases of the negative half and of integrable highest
weight modules, proves the based-quotient presentation
$\pi_\lambda:U_A^-\twoheadrightarrow V_A(\lambda)$, relates the
normalized quasi-$R$ intertwiner $\Theta$ to the Drinfeld pairing $D$, and
computes the tensor bars on finite products in exactly the admissible
classes.

**Scope and dependence.** The page is the globalization layer of
[[divided-powers-integral-forms-and-quantum-highest-weights]],
[[kashiwara-operators-and-crystal-lattices]] and
[[tensor-product-crystals-and-highest-weight-crystal-uniqueness]]: it
imports the divided-power integral form, the Kashiwara lattices and
operators, the grand loop and the crystal tensor rule, and it proves the
integral balancedness, freeness, base change and duality statements that
those pages leave open. The in-run prerequisites supply the normalized half form, the integrable
highest weight module and the local $q=1$ comparison. Their exact hypotheses
and conclusions are used in the items below. The historical supplier defects
recorded in `research/frontier-44-special-representation-examples-28-six-step-reader-8.md`
were corrected; the current proofs are reviewed separately in
`research/frontier-44-special-representation-examples-28-six-step-alpha-batch-8-3a.md`.

## Normalizations and the two charts

The page begins with the convention dictionary
[[lem-lusztig-and-kashiwara-normalizations-match-by-root-color]], which
transports Lusztig's parameter $v=q^{-1}$ to the library's Drinfeld-Jimbo
presentation, matches the coproducts up to the tensor flip, and computes
the exact root-color factor $B_L=C_\nu B_K$ between the source and
normalized half forms. The local chart algebra is isolated in
[[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]] and
[[def-balanced-triple-and-globalization-map]], with the integral residue
lattices of
[[def-integral-residue-lattices-of-the-negative-half-and-highest-weight-modules]]
and the projective-line form of the lifting criterion proved in
[[lem-balanced-triple-linear-algebra-over-the-projective-line]]: a finite
free simultaneous lift module generating the integral module over $A$, with
injective images in both chart residues, is what
turns a triple into a balanced triple, and the relative form of the
criterion applies modulo an already balanced submodule.

## The quasi-$R$ intertwiner and the Drinfeld pairing

The normalized Drinfeld pairing is defined in
[[def-drinfeld-hopf-pairing-between-positive-and-negative-quantum-halves]]
and proved perfect in each root degree in
[[lem-the-drinfeld-hopf-pairing-is-nondegenerate-in-each-root-degree]].
The diagonal root-height completion of
[[def-root-height-completion-for-weightwise-quasi-r-intertwiners]] and the
dual-basis sums of
[[lem-homogeneous-dual-basis-sums-are-basis-independent-and-weightwise-finite]]
then make sense of the quasi-$R$ family, and
[[thm-the-weightwise-quasi-r-intertwiner-exists-and-is-unique]] identifies
it as the unique normalized bar-coproduct intertwiner
$\Delta(u)\Theta=\Theta\bar\Delta(u)$ with its two generator recursions
and the rank-one coefficient $(q_i-q_i^{-1})^n[n]_{q_i^2}!$. Its inverse
and coproduct factorizations, including the field cocycle, are
[[lem-quasi-r-intertwining-determines-the-inverse-and-coproduct-factorizations]],
used later for the tensor construction.

## Integral string ideals and their balance

The negative-half input is organized by the string ideals
$I_{(i,n)}^A=U_A^-\cap F_i^nU_q^-$ and their module images: the integral
projector, the adapted decompositions and the boundary-generation identity
are [[lem-string-ideal-decomposition-of-the-integral-lattices]], the
saturation of integral lattice intersections under the reversal
anti-involution is [[lem-negative-half-reversal-preserves-integral-and-crystal-lattices]],
and the induction step that balances every string ideal from the
lower-height hypotheses is [[lem-string-ideal-triples-are-balanced]]. The
integral crystal residues that these ideals compute are identified with
the $\mathbb Z$-spans of the crystal sets in
[[lem-integral-crystal-residues-of-the-negative-half-represent-the-crystal-basis]].

## Globalization

[[thm-the-highest-weight-crystal-triple-is-balanced]] is the main induction:
it produces the balanced triples of $U_A^-$ and of every $V_A(\lambda)$,
the bar-invariant lower global bases $G_\infty(b),G_\lambda(b)$, the free
$A$-bases with their classical ranks, the string-ideal decompositions and
the exact top-string transition
$G_\infty(\tilde f_i^nb)-F_i^{(n)}G_\infty(b)\in I_{(i,n+1)}^A$.
[[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]] and
[[thm-existence-bar-invariance-and-uniqueness-of-the-lower-global-basis]]
record the definition and the uniqueness that every later consumer uses,
and [[thm-global-basis-projection-from-the-negative-half-to-a-highest-weight-module]]
proves that the projection $\pi_\lambda$ is a based quotient over
$\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$, with the exact integral kernel
$\sum_i\sum_{s>\lambda(h_i)}U_A^-F_i^{(s)}$.

The form-dual side is developed in
[[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]] and
[[thm-upper-and-lower-global-bases-are-dual-and-crystal-compatible]]:
restricted graded perfectness of the integral pairing, the genuine dual
charts, adjoint bar invariance and the exact weighted mixed adjunctions of
the upper operators. Two structural consequences follow:
[[thm-integral-triangular-decomposition-for-the-lusztig-form]] proves the
integral triangular decomposition and freeness of the Lusztig form, and
[[prop-global-bases-specialize-to-integral-weight-bases]] and
[[thm-quantum-highest-weight-modules-deform-the-classical-weight-character]]
compute base change and the characteristic-zero $q=1$ fibre with the
classical Weyl-Kac character. The symmetric finite ADE comparison with Lusztig's
canonical basis is
[[thm-lusztig-canonical-and-kashiwara-global-bases-agree-in-symmetric-type]],
proved by the signed norm characterization, the exact $T_{i,n}$
top-string recursion and the based quotient.

## Tensor bars

The final layer transfers the quasi-$R$ action to tensor products:
[[lem-quasi-r-divided-power-integrality-on-based-lattices]] develops the
integral action in the stated highest-first, lowest-second, finite-type
and $C_{\mathrm{high}}/C_{\mathrm{low}}$ cases, with the
affine counterexample showing that the unrestricted arbitrary-based
assertion fails, and
[[thm-quasi-r-tensor-bars-on-finite-products-of-based-integrable-modules]]
turns this into the well-defined semilinear tensor bar, its triangular
weight transfer and the corrected tensor global basis in the admissible
cases. Both items keep the distinction between the raw tensor products of
lower basis vectors and the corrected bar-fixed lifts. The local action-finiteness
and supported-correction prerequisites for arbitrary finite-type based modules
remain open review obligations, recorded in
`research/frontier-44-special-representation-examples-28-six-step-alpha-batch-8-3a.md`.

## Choice

The Axiom of Choice is declared once in the prerequisite pages and
propagates through the grand-loop, negative-half-form and generic PBW-rank suppliers;
each item above states its exact use. The chart lemmas, the string-ideal
inductions, the dual-basis and tensor-correction computations are
choice-free, and no item on this page uses AC for any statement not already
carrying it.

## How to read this page

Items are ordered by dependency level and then by page order. The first
group fixes normalizations, charts and the quasi-$R$ calculus; the second
proves the integral balancedness and globalization; the third develops
duality, specialization and the canonical comparison; the last two treat
the tensor action, its exact scope and its boundary counterexamples. The
companion page [[balanced-triples-and-global-crystal-bases-examples]] works
the same machinery on the smallest explicit lattices and on the two known
failure modes.

**Objective.** This page is the convention bridge between the quantum-group
level-one Fock space of [[quantum-affine-type-a-and-level-one-fock-space]] and
the modular good-node crystal of
[[modular-branching-and-the-good-node-crystal]]. It fixes the residue
convention, compares the two residue readings of a node signature and
transports the Fock module, its crystal and its global basis into the
symmetric-group convention. No quantum affine relation, semi-infinite wedge or
Misra-Miwa crystal is re-derived here: those constructions remain on the
quantum-group page, and this page only compares their output with the modular
branching combinatorics.

**The convention.** [[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]]
fixes a finite quantum characteristic $e \ge 2$ at charge $0$, lists the
addable and removable nodes of a residue top to bottom, defines the modular
reduced signature with good $=$ first surviving $-$ and cogood $=$ last
surviving $+$, records the dictionary between $e$-restricted and $e$-regular
partitions, and introduces the linear transport $J M_\lambda = |\lambda'\rangle$
with its reflected colors and reflected weights. The boundary $e = 0$ is
proved there by the distinct-content corner argument, with the source label
convention recorded separately.

**The comparison.** [[lem-level-one-node-order-and-conjugation-dictionary]]
proves that on the nodes of one residue the top-to-bottom order is the
decreasing-content and decreasing-column order, and that conjugation reverses
the reading order while preserving signs; this is the order dictionary between
the modular top-to-bottom reduction and the Fock-space increasing-content
reduction. [[prop-qg-fock-crystal-arrows-agree-with-the-modular-good-node-operators]]
then shows that conjugation carries the modular good-node and cogood-node
operators exactly onto the normalized Fock-space operators with negated colors,
including zero values, and identifies the survivor counts with the normal and
conormal node counts. Neither convention swaps deletion with addition: good is
removable and cogood is addable on both sides, and ordinary Chevalley
coefficients, in particular negative powers, are not the arrows.

**The restricted component.** [[thm-restricted-partition-component-is-the-basic-crystal-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]]
proves that the empty component of the transported full Fock crystal is exactly
the $e$-restricted partitions, that it is the basic crystal $B(\Lambda_0)$
generated from the empty partition by cogood additions, that the full crystal is
reducible with the transported partition-number decomposition, and that in the
symmetric-group regime of prime characteristic the good-node restriction of a
James-labelled simple has the transposed deleted label as its simple socle.

**Global bases.** [[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]]
transports the lower global basis of the basic representation and defines its
transition polynomials in the symmetric-group labelling, together with the
weightwise ambient Gram matrix and the upper vectors in the basic subspace.
Their standard-frame coordinates are rational in general, while the vectors
form the exact integral upper basis in their own restricted dual lattice; the
normalized form identification and the perfect pairing with the lower span
are proved locally using the global-basis suppliers. Lower and upper integral
lattices and their ambient coordinates are distinguished throughout, and no
specialization to Hecke decomposition numbers is asserted here.

This page develops the modular branching theory of the symmetric groups in
the residue convention $\operatorname{res}(r,c)=c-r\bmod p$ and in the
$p$-restricted labelling of the simple modules, and isolates the
good-node combinatorics as a self-contained crystal. The first layer fixes
the objects that make the branching computable inside $kS_n$: the
Jucys-Murphy elements $L_1,\dots,L_n$ of
[[def-jucys-murphy-elements-of-the-symmetric-group-algebra]] are used to
split the regular representation into simultaneous primary components, and
the resulting central content idempotents cut the restriction and induction
functors into residue summands $E_i$ and $F_i$. These functors are the
algebro-group-free form of the residue decomposition of the branching
problem; they are exact, additive, duality-compatible and available over an
arbitrary field of characteristic $p$, with no splitting hypothesis beyond
the fact that symmetric groups are split over their prime field. On the
combinatorial side, [[def-residue-signature-normal-good-conormal-and-cogood-nodes]]
fixes the residue signature of the $i$-nodes of a $p$-restricted partition,
the cancellation of $(-,+)$ pairs and the resulting notions of normal,
good, conormal and cogood nodes, together with the counts
$\varepsilon_i,\varphi_i$, and it records the transposed-node dictionary
that relates this convention to Brundan's $\ell$-residue $r-c$.
[[def-good-node-and-cogood-node-crystal-operators]] turns the good and
cogood nodes into partial operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ on
$p$-restricted partitions and proves, purely combinatorially, that they are
mutually inverse and change the rank by one.

The second layer connects the functors with the nodes.
[[lem-finite-group-induction-is-coinduction-and-thus-biadjoint]] records the
relative Frobenius isomorphism $\operatorname{Ind}\cong\operatorname{Coind}$
for a subgroup of a finite group, so that induction is both a left and a
right adjoint of restriction in the modular setting.
[[cor-socle-of-uncoloured-modular-restriction-is-the-sum-over-good-residues]]
states the residue-refined socle theorem for $D(\mu)\downarrow_{S_{d-1}}$:
the socle is the multiplicity-free sum of the simples $D(\mu\setminus A_i)$
over the good nodes, one for each residue with $\varepsilon_i(\mu)>0$. From
this, [[prop-every-p-restricted-partition-is-reached-by-cogood-node-additions]]
derives the connectivity of the modular branching graph: every
$p$-restricted partition is reached from the empty partition by cogood-node
additions, equivalently by good-node deletions. A remark draws the boundary
of what is proved here: the identification of the cellular labels with the
crystal labels is not an elementary consequence of the combinatorics and is
used only where separately stated, so no circularity enters the induction
on rank.

The third layer compares the branching multiplicities with the first-level
multiplicities over the algebraic group and with the Hecke algebra.
[[prop-schur-functor-compares-first-level-branching-with-hecke-restriction]]
uses the type-A $q$-Schur algebra and its Schur functor to identify the
Schur image of the first level of a simple module with the restriction of the corresponding
Hecke simple module, and transfers composition multiplicities between the
first level and the Hecke restriction; the comparison is stated at general
quantum characteristic and specialized to $q=1$.
[[thm-kleshchev-first-level-branching-multiplicity]] records Kleshchev's
first-level branching multiplicity: for a removable node $A$ of a
$p$-regular partition the multiplicity of $D^{\lambda(j)}$ in the
restriction is zero when $A$ is not normal and is one plus the number of
normal nodes strictly above $A$ in the same residue class when $A$ is
normal. The next two theorems give the residue-restriction and
residue-induction multiplicities: the multiplicity of $D(\mu\setminus A)$
in $E_iD(\mu)$ for a normal node $A$ counts the normal nodes weakly below
$A$ when $A$ is normal (and is zero otherwise), and, dually, the multiplicity of $D(\mu\cup B)$ in $F_iD(\mu)$ for a
conormal node $B$ counts the conormal nodes weakly above $B$. The layer
closes with the socle and head theorems for the extreme nodes: if $A$ is
the good node then $E_iD(\mu)$ has simple socle and head $D(\mu\setminus A)$
occurring with multiplicity $\varepsilon_i(\mu)$, and if $B$ is the cogood
node then $F_iD(\mu)$ has simple socle and head $D(\mu\cup B)$ occurring
with multiplicity $\varphi_i(\mu)$.

Throughout, $k$ is a field of characteristic $p>0$, all partitions in the
crystal statements are $p$-restricted unless stated otherwise, all
residues are read as $c-r\bmod p$ with nodes ordered top to bottom, and
every item is finite-dimensional and choice-free, with the characteristic
$2$ case included. The page records the source theorems it uses (Kleshchev's
survey and 1997 paper, and Brundan's 1998 paper) by exact locators; the
local proofs and their declared suppliers carry the mathematical arguments.

This page develops the cellular-algebra foundations of the modular
representation theory of the type-A Hecke algebra and its q-Schur algebra. It
begins with the Graham-Lehrer cellular calculus, the cell form and its radical,
and the classification of the simple modules by the nonzero cell heads
$D^{\lambda}=C^{\lambda}/\mathrm{rad}\,C^{\lambda}$, with the
dominance-unitriangular decomposition matrix as its first consequence.

The second half specialises to $H_{F,q}(S_n)$: the Murphy cellular basis and
the identification of the Hecke Specht modules through the Dipper-James
signed-cell dictionary, the triangular action of the Jucys-Murphy elements and
the resulting seminormal bases in the separated range, the classification of
the simple modules by the $e$-regular partitions, and the Schur functor
connecting Weyl modules and their Jantzen filtrations to Specht modules. The
q-Schaper virtual radical-layer formula and its hook-product Gram determinants
are recorded in the form needed by the block and decomposition-number items of
later pages, together with an explicit remark on the limits of what
cellularity and the sum formula determine.
